primary_topics: Response remarks by CJP at an FEU 80th anniversary book launch event, January 22, 2008 -- after Justice Carpio's lecture and Salonga and Miranda-Feliciano's book presentations; CJ Puno sent a letter of apology for his absence

Individual tributes to seven people: FEU Chair Dr. Lourdes Reyes Montinola (Forbes 40 richest; friend since student days); FEU President Dr. Lydia Echauz (dynamo partner); Dr. Raul Pangalangan (the unpromoted SC potential); the Panganiban Court colleagues (Morales, Azcuna, Sandoval-Gutierrez, Carpio); Mrs. Evelyn Miranda-Feliciano; and Senator Salonga

The UP-vs-FEU joke: since UP graduates constitute the majority of Philippine presidents, cabinet members and justices, why is the Philippines still plagued by corruption and poverty? 'Because not all the UP graduates became FEU deans, like Sen. Salonga'

The Raul Pangalangan observation: 'that he has not been appointed to the Supreme Court yet is not a reflection of his lack of credentials; rather, it reflects the lack of ability of the appointing authority to recognize talent, intellectual gravitas, and courage in a truly outstanding lawyer and academic'
sub_topics: CJ Puno's absence: 'Chief Justice Reynato S. Puno has written a letter expressing his inability to attend our launching today due to a prior commitment'
FEU claim: 'Far Eastern University, the best school in the world, according to the FEU Alumni Association and me'

UP-vs-FEU joke: a senator-friend recently wrote that UP graduates constitute the majority of former presidents, cabinet members, senators, congressmen and SC justices; CJP: 'If that were so, how come the Philippines is still plagued by rampant corruption, unmitigated violence, grinding poverty, and extralegal killings? Aha, because not all the UP graduates became FEU deans, like Sen. Salonga.'

Dr. Lourdes Reyes Montinola: Forbes 40 richest Filipinos; 'has risked her fortune, time, effort and name in elevating FEU to new educational heights'; CJP met her when he was a student leader and she was the corporate secretary of the University
Dr. Lydia Echauz: 'the dynamo partner of Dr. Montinola in energizing and electrifying the deans, faculty and students of FEU'

Dr. Raul Pangalangan: 'chair of Bantay Katarungan, former UP law dean, favorite exchange professor of Harvard Law School. That he has not been appointed to the Supreme Court yet is not a reflection of his lack of credentials for the job; rather, it reflects the lack of ability of the appointing authority to recognize talent, intellectual gravitas, and courage in a truly outstanding lawyer and academic.'
Panganiban Court colleagues: Justice Conchita Carpio Morales, Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna, Justice Angelina Sandoval-Gutierrez, Justice Antonio T. Carpio (guest speaker)

Salonga: 'I first met Senate President Salonga more than fifty years ago when he was my professor and dean at the FEU Institute of Law. Since then up to the present, he has become my lifetime mentor and guru not only in the labyrinths of the law but more important, on how to enjoy a life worth living.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered January 22, 2008 as CJP's response remarks at an FEU 80th anniversary book launch -- after Justice Antonio Carpio's lecture and the book presentations by Senator Jovito Salonga and Mrs. Evelyn Miranda-Feliciano; CJ Puno sent an apology letter -- this address is a sequence of individual tributes punctuated by wit. It opens with the claim that FEU is 'the best school in the world, according to the FEU Alumni Association and me,' and the UP-vs-FEU joke: since UP produces most Philippine presidents, cabinet members and justices, why is the country still plagued by corruption and poverty? 'Aha, because not all the UP graduates became FEU deans, like Sen. Salonga.' CJP thanks FEU Chair Dr. Lourdes Reyes Montinola (Forbes 40 richest Filipinos; met her when she was corporate secretary and he was a student leader; 'has risked her fortune, time, effort and name in elevating FEU to new educational heights'); FEU President Dr. Lydia Echauz ('the dynamo partner of Dr. Montinola in energizing and electrifying the deans, faculty and students'); Dr. Raul Pangalangan (Bantay Katarungan chair; former UP law dean; Harvard's favorite exchange professor; 'that he has not been appointed to the Supreme Court yet is not a reflection of his lack of credentials; rather, it reflects the lack of ability of the appointing authority to recognize talent, intellectual gravitas, and courage'); Panganiban Court colleagues Justices Conchita Carpio Morales, Adolfo Azcuna, Angelina Sandoval-Gutierrez and Antonio Carpio; Mrs. Miranda-Feliciano; and Senator Salonga: 'I first met him more than fifty years ago when he was my professor and dean at FEU. Since then he has become my lifetime mentor and guru not only in the labyrinths of the law but more important, on how to enjoy a life worth living.'
